refinedBaseNodes.label: AssignmentPlanner
refinedBaseNodes.refinement: Local Assignment planning now acquires the Task's unique LOCAL_ASSIGNMENT execution claim atomically with Assignment creation.

refinedBaseNodes.label: SemanticVerifier
refinedBaseNodes.refinement: Remote digest-verified artifact evidence is normalized into the existing EvidenceBundle and evaluated by the existing EvidenceSemanticVerifier rather than a remote-specific semantic rule set.

discoveredNodes.label: TaskExecutionClaimStore
discoveredNodes.reason: One Task must have exactly one execution owner so local Runtime work and remote delegated delivery cannot both execute the same semantic Task.

discoveredNodes.label: ClaimAwareAssignmentPlanner
discoveredNodes.reason: Local Assignment creation and LOCAL_ASSIGNMENT ownership must be one transaction.

discoveredNodes.label: ClaimAwareDeliveryCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: A remote Binding must own execution before the external send effect; response loss keeps fail-closed ownership and exact retry identity.

discoveredNodes.label: RemoteArtifactReader
discoveredNodes.reason: Remote artifact transport/provider access is replaceable and returns explicit artifact identity, kind, digest and content.

discoveredNodes.label: RemoteArtifactEvidenceResolver
discoveredNodes.reason: Remote bytes must pass identity/kind/digest checks before they become normalized EvidenceBundle facts.

discoveredNodes.label: RemoteTaskVerificationStore
discoveredNodes.reason: Remote semantic/mechanical verification requires a durable exact receipt distinct from Runtime Assignment verification.

discoveredNodes.label: RemoteTaskCompletionReconciler
discoveredNodes.reason: Remote provider terminal state becomes local Task truth only through local mechanical/evidence/semantic verification.

flow: LOCAL path -> N59 ClaimAwareAssignmentPlanner -> existing Runtime/evidence pipeline
REMOTE path -> R9 TransportBinding -> N60 ClaimAwareDeliveryCoordinator
authorityLaws: Each Task has at most one durable execution claim.
LOCAL_ASSIGNMENT and REMOTE_BINDING claims are mutually exclusive.
DelegationEnvelope and multiple TransportBindings are intent/route candidates; they do not own execution until one remote Binding is delivered.
The first remote Binding to execute claims the Task and all alternate/fallback Bindings fail closed until an explicit future claim-transfer protocol exists.
Remote execution claim is committed before the external send effect, so response loss cannot reopen the Task for local or fallback double execution.
Exact retry after remote response loss reuses the same Binding/delivery_request_id while retaining the same execution claim.
Goal dependency readiness is enforced before a remote Binding can claim a Goal-managed Task.
Remote delivery moves the local Task to RUNNING but does not complete it.
Remote provider terminal/success remains observation evidence; the Task remains RUNNING until RemoteTaskCompletionReconciler verifies it.
Remote successful execution requires digest-verified artifact evidence before semantic acceptance is evaluated.
Remote artifact identity mismatch, digest mismatch, missing/ambiguous artifact kind, or missing reader fails closed without creating a Task verdict.
Remote provider mechanical failure may produce a local FAILED verdict only through a durable remote verification record, not directly from RemoteDeliveryObserver.
Remote semantic verification reuses the existing EvidenceSemanticVerifier to avoid a second acceptance authority.
Remote verification receipts persist provenance/digest metadata and do not persist raw remote artifact content.
R10 DeliveryReceipts created before execution claims existed can be adopted by R11 without re-sending the remote effect; adoption creates the REMOTE_BINDING claim and converges Task state to RUNNING.
Execution-claim release/transfer is intentionally not implemented in R11; safe failover remains a future explicit protocol.
compatibilityDebt: The frozen acceptance kind runtime_artifact_text_contains is reused for remote artifact semantic verification in R11. The resolver is remote-specific, but renaming the acceptance kind to a transport-neutral name is deferred to a dedicated schema migration.
